Excel finite-result, fifteen-digit comparison, ROUND and root-addition policies reuse the existing format decimal owner. Root Arithmetic::apply_float now owns the operation kernel used by generic floating Scalars and the Excel adapter; no Term is parsed or bound per cell.

Temporal calendar parts now share one native accessor between ISO formatting and generic expression extraction, preserving existing timezone/year/null semantics without formatting a string for each row. Scalar::calendar_parts owns value extraction.
Generic expression abs is a typed redirect to Scalar::checked_abs. Existing Arrow fallback shares that evaluator; statistics stay conservative. Null and encoded-null outputs remain nullable.

The explicit-stack workbook evaluator now handles constant arithmetic and numeric ABS through shared core kernels. Cache publication is staged atomically; temporal results use the existing serial conversion and array/data-table/dynamic-array anchors retain their caches.
Numeric entry now shares the stack-based fifteen-digit decimal intake owner with formula literals; no temporary decimal String is allocated.

The sparse dependency index stores rectangles once, with exclusive owner-stamped registration handles, canonical axis buckets and borrowed zero-allocation point-query cursors. Scheduling uses Kahn plus iterative SCC classification without retained edge lists; Workbook integration is pending.

Subnormal addition/subtraction results are explicitly uncomputed until raw in-memory results can be represented separately from saved XML caches; multiplication/division/percent retain their separately native-confirmed zero behavior.
1904 negative date/time rendering uses the magnitude and selected section sign policy, while the 1900 system refuses negative dates. Both use the existing DateSystem upper bound.

Ordered numeric SUM now uses one constant-space Accumulator over shared Arithmetic, with native-confirmed final-pair cancellation and explicit-error precedence. Numeric ROUND redirects to the calibrated decimal primitive. Origin-sensitive coercions and references remain held pending their own integration.

Generic SQRT resolves and casts its numeric argument once in the existing expression binder, then redirects to Scalar::checked_sqrt. The Excel adapter calls that same Float64 kernel and handles Excel domain errors separately; no generic Term is constructed per cell.

All native decimal scalar layouts now use Arrow's exported decimal-to-float primitive at the matching coefficient width. Generic explicit casts and Excel reference adapters share this allocation-free owner; no per-value Arrow array or decimal string is built.

Direct Excel operands reuse Entry's numeric and temporal intake. Unary plus preserves operand type; numeric consumers apply Excel coercion at this boundary. All 108 direct native controls match result types and exact bits. Referenced/array coercion still awaits context integration.
Sheet change tracking stays inactive until needed, reuses distinct pending-point capacity, and restores marks through nested Workbook attempts without additional checkpoint allocation.

Workbook now retains the sparse dependency graph, schedule, evaluator and bounded scratch. calculate_all forces all nodes; recalculate updates changed point dependencies and evaluates the dirty closure. Source references and range consumers share legacy-intersection geometry; cycle reports distinguish actual SCC members from blocked dependents.

A formula reference reads the same published cache domain during full and incremental passes. Blank results become numeric zero; unresolved temporal serials consistently remain held. The Cell operand owner supplies both paths, preserving exact General numeric bits and text/Boolean/error types.

Legacy scalar/range behavior matches 38 native observations for both authored and Excel-saved formula spellings. The supported numeric reference paths match 94 native coercion cases; blank-versus-empty-text equality matches two additional native cases and symmetric/nonempty controls.
